newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Yukong cuts petrol price to lowest in S.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Yukong cuts petrol price to lowest in S.Korea.

text.p: South Korea's Yukong Ltd said on Monday it had dropped its retail petrol prices to 823 won per litre from 829 won -- the lowest level offered by the country's refiners.
"We have lowered our petrol price to dismiss our image as a company that sells the most expensive petrol and to show appreciation to our fixed customers," a company spokesman said.
Yukong has had the highest retail pump prices in South Korea among the refining sector since domestic prices were deregulated on January 1.

Yukong's previous price of 829 won was higher than the 826 won charged by Ssangyong Oil Refining Co, Hyundai Oil Refinery Co and Hanwha Energy Co Ltd. LG-Caltex Oil Corp has been selling petrol for 829 won.
The spokesman said its price cut would hurt other oil companies.
"It's not intentional, but the price cut would deal a severe blow to other oil refiners because we have such a large number of the petrol stations."
Yukong has the largest share of domestic petrol market at 37.5 percent, analysts said. It also has the biggest refining capacity of 810,000 barrels per day.
Refiners raised petrol prices in the two months following deregulation. But with crude oil prices falling, they have started cutting prices.
